title: Book 5 — Terpsichore, Chapter 101
paragraphs: From plundering the city after they had taken it, they were prevented by this: the houses in Sardis were mostly built of reeds, and even those of them that were of brick had their roofs thatched with reeds. One of these houses was set on fire by a soldier, and the fire, spreading from house to house, began to take the whole town. As the town burned, the Lydians and all the Persians in the city, cut off from escape since the fire prevailed around them on every side and they had no way out, gathered together in the marketplace and along the river Pactolus—which brings them down gold-dust from Tmolus, flowing through the middle of their marketplace, and then empties into the river Hermus, which in turn empties into the sea. To this Pactolus, I say, and to the marketplace the Lydians and Persians gathered, and were compelled to defend themselves. Then the Ionians, seeing some of the enemy standing on their defense and others in great numbers coming up to attack, were struck with fear and withdrew to the mountain called Tmolus, and at nightfall went off to their ships.
